The table places four figures side by side precisely to show their methodological differences: global modelling, records-based surveillance, reported diagnosis in a survey and a population-survey estimate. Its function is to teach comparison, not to decide which country ‘has more autism’.
Do not rank countries from highest to lowest and do not call every column ‘prevalence’. Each figure uses different ages, methods and denominators.
The figure must remain linked to its population, territory, year and method. Separating it from that context can change its meaning.
